[00:00] Mark: okay, uh, thanks everyone for joining, we've got about 45 minutes. quick roll call?
[00:10] Oliver: Oliver here, Maya here, Leo on as well.
[00:14] Mark: cool, Mark from Redwood, Priya, Samir with me. We'll go through the CSV results you shared last night and then the eviction churn anomaly.
[00:22] Priya: yes, I'll start with the hit rates snapshot, i pulled the sheet into the call. um you might see some weird buckets — some cohort traffic is extremely bursty.
[00:30] [00:30] Priya: overall KV cache global hit-rate is at ~37% after prefetch v2, prefix reuse gives another 9% effective token reuse, so combined reduction is about 46% tokens saved on the sampled workload. (faint) that's averaged, cohort A is 62% hit on warm hours, cohort C is like 8%, so big variance.
[00:50] Maya: question — when you say "prefetch v2" which one is that? the one that prefetches full 64-token prefix or the trimmed one?
[00:55] Priya: good call, that's the trimmed 24-token prefetch. we switched from full prefix prefetch to trimmed prefix + metadata-key hashing to reduce false positives.
[01:05] Leo: i saw the CSV comments about the "prefetch window" can you explain what that parameter does again?
[01:12] Priya: sure. window is how many tokens from the start of session we attempt to match and load into KV up front. 24 tokens here means we target the first 24 tokens and any matching prefix signature loads the KV entries.
[01:25] Oliver: and eviction policy? we're running LRU with a custom threshold?
[01:28] Priya: yes, currently LRU-0.6 across the pool in the pilot cluster. We introduced a soft-eviction thermostat that prefers keeping prefixes with high recent reuse.
[01:36] Mark: just to surface, we noticed high eviction churn in cohort B which corresponds to your low-latency bursty chat endpoints — those have a short TTL and frequent new prefixes.
[01:45] Maya: yeah that's the critical one for us, it's the chat assist front-end. We saw latency spikes when the eviction thrash happens.
[01:52] Priya: right, the eviction thrash leads to KV misses and more CPU/GPU cycles, raising p95 by about 120ms in that trace set.
[02:02] [02:02] Oliver: hmm 120ms is big for us, we need sub-200 p95 for chat. is that with prefetch on?
[02:08] Priya: yes with prefetch enabled, because prefetch can increase insertion pressure if many false-positive matches occur, which in turn increases compaction/eviction.
[02:18] Mark: i want to underline that tradeoff — more prefetch increases hit-rate when matches are real, but on high-entropy traffic it increases churn and cost.
[02:26] Leo: can we do a hybrid? only prefetch for sessions flagged as repeat users or high similarity?
[02:31] Priya: that is precisely what we tested in the AB hybrid set: prefetch-by-signal, where traffic with flagged user-id similarity uses prefetch, others are on-demand. initial results were promising for cohort A but mixed for cohort B.
[02:45] Maya: what's the false-positive rate on the prefix signatures? i.e., prefetch that loads wrong KV entries?
[02:52] Priya: measured ~3.4% false-positive signature matches across entire sample, but for cohort B it's closer to 9% due to lots of short, similar prefixes.
[03:02] [03:02] Mark: ok let's dig into the "eviction anomaly" logs you shared — Priya, you had a plot showing eviction spikes every 20 minutes?
[03:09] Priya: yes i do, it's in the sheet. essentially the pilot cluster does periodic compaction when memory crosses 78%, and with bursty arrivals compaction coincides with high insert rates so we get a compaction+eviction wave.
[03:22] Oliver: is that a runtime behavior we can tune? 
[03:25] Priya: yes, two knobs: compaction threshold and target-reserve memory. and a smarter eviction policy — we can add an adaptive decay factor so newly inserted entries are less likely to evict high reuse entries.
[03:37] Maya: can the decay be per-prefix-type? some prefixes (system prompts) are definitely long-lived.
[03:42] Priya: yes we can tag by prefix-type and apply different decay constants. that is part of the config-diff I prepared.
[03:49] Leo: are there any changes to our SLA or cost when we increase reserve memory?
[03:53] Mark: slight increase in memory footprint on the Dedicated pool, which may bump cost if you expand the pool size. but it's a tradeoff vs p95 savings. we can run a cost-projection.
[04:02] [04:02] Oliver: will the Dedicated vs Hosted choice affect this? we're currently on Dedicated pilot cluster, right?
[04:07] Mark: yes dedicated. Hosted would offer autoscaling but less control over eviction policies; Dedicated gives you more tunability.
[04:14] Maya: about security, we've got legal wanting confirmation on data residency and KMS. Mark, did you send the SOC2 snapshot?
[04:20] Mark: i'll send the SOC2 export and the security-answers.pdf; we also support KMS integration — note there's an extra step for on-prem HSM if you go that route.
[04:28] Oliver: okay good.
[04:30] [04:30] Priya: back to performance — i want to propose three short experiments for next week: 1) raise compaction threshold to 84% and observe eviction churn, 2) enable per-prefix decay tagging for cohort B, 3) reduce prefetch window to 16 tokens for cohort B.
[04:45] Maya: sounds reasonable. what's the expected effect of reducing to 16 tokens?
[04:49] Priya: reduces false-positive signature matches, so fewer insertions and less churn; may reduce hit-rate for sessions that need longer contexts.
[04:58] Leo: do we have a runbook for toggling these live? i.e., rollback steps?
[05:03] Priya: yes, config-diff includes rollback flags and a safe-fallback policy to disable prefetch per-route if errors exceed a threshold.
[05:12] [05:12] Oliver: earlier you mentioned prefix hashing — are there collisions that could cause bad KV retrievals?
[05:18] Priya: collision rate is very low; most mismatches are due to short prefixes that look similar, not real hash collisions.
[05:25] Mark: can i ask about metrics we should watch? Priya suggested p95 token latency, KV insert rate, eviction count/min, and net tokens saved. Anything to add?
[05:35] Maya: include GPU token-per-second and CPU scheduling queue length.
[05:38] Priya: and hit-rate per prefix-length bucket is key.
[05:42] [05:42] Oliver: okay let's talk about the hybrid AB results you referenced — what's the confidence interval?
[05:47] Priya: AB was run on a 48h window; cohort A showed 18% lower token cost with no latency regression, cohort B saw 3% cost reduction but p95 regressed by 90ms. CI for B is wide due to burstiness.
[06:02] Leo: can we do signal improvements? we have user similarity scoring; maybe combine that with prefix-signature confidence.
[06:09] Priya: yep, a weighted ensemble of user-sim + signature-confidence is what we'd recommend. that's low-effort to implement as a prefilter.
[06:17] [06:17] Samir: on the customer success side, if we can stabilize cohort B with the three experiments, what's the run-of-show to go to pilot->production?
[06:25] Mark: typical ramp is 2-week expanded pilot, then small prod rollout (10% traffic), monitor 7 days, then full rollout. we usually require you to hit target p95 and cost delta thresholds.
[06:35] Oliver: what's the target cost delta you're looking for?
[06:37] Mark: we had a agreed target of >=12% token cost reduction at parity p95, but we can rebaseline for chat if that's unrealistic.
[06:45] Maya: i also want to raise the point about billing and metering — how do we attribute token savings across teams?
[06:51] Mark: we can provide per-route token breakdown in Console; you can map routes to product teams for chargeback. that data is in the dashboard export we shared.
[06:59] [06:59] Priya: quick note: there's a weird artifact in the CSV labelled "prefetch-dup" which is double-counting some sessions; i'm going to clean that up and re-run the numbers.
[07:07] Oliver: ah that might explain discrepancy with our internal numbers.
[07:11] Priya: yes i'll update and push a corrected CSV by end of day.
[07:16] [07:16] Mark: perfect. next i wanted to surface a small security ask — your legal asked for SSO/SAML details and audit log retention periods. we have docs but i can attach them.
[07:26] Oliver: please do, our auditors need timeline.
[07:29] [07:29] Priya: back to tuning — i want to propose a slightly different eviction policy experiment: adaptive-LRU that multiplies eviction score by recent-reuse-window. preliminary sim shows reduction in evictions by 24% for long-lived prefixes.
[07:43] Maya: sounds promising, do we need code changes in runtime?
[07:46] Priya: just a config toggle + a tiny runtime flag; no heavy kernel work. can be shipped in patch.
[07:52] Leo: good. any risk to correctness? we need to ensure we don't keep stale user-specific prompts.
[07:57] Priya: we tag entries by sessionID type and apply time-based TTL overrides for sensitive prompts.
[08:05] [08:05] Oliver: okay, time check — we have 40 minutes left, maybe walk through the CSV anomalies quickly?
[08:10] Priya: sure, page to sheet tab "anomalies" — row 112 has churn spike correlated with heavy compaction at 2026-06-15T03:40Z.
[08:20] Maya: that timestamp corresponds to a deploy we did on the product side, might be correlated.
[08:24] Oliver: good catch, we'll cross-check deploy logs.
[08:27] Priya: also in row 210 there's a repeated insert pattern from a bot user sending slightly different prompts. that's inflating unique-prefix counts.
[08:36] [08:36] Leo: can we blacklist or throttle such noisy actors at ingress? that would help.
[08:40] Priya: yes, ingress throttles or request deduplication is effective; we can add a prefilter rule to your gateway.
[08:47] Mark: on the action item side, we'll help with a gateway rule example.

[08:58] Mark: the config-diff is portable across Dedicated and Private; we can package as a feature flag toggle for your staging cluster.
[09:05] Priya: i'll produce a 'staging safe' config set with conservative defaults.
[09:10] [09:10] Maya: excellent.
[09:12] Mark: ok, let's prioritize the three experiments: compaction threshold bump, per-prefix decay for cohort B, reduce prefetch window for cohort B. We'll run them sequentially to isolate effects.
[09:22] Priya: proposed schedule: start compaction threshold on Thursday 06/18, observe 24h; then per-prefix decay Monday 06/22; then prefetch window tweak Wed 06/24.
[09:32] Oliver: sounds good, but can we swap order if initial results are bad?
